page: Google Cloud Platform c4n-highcpu-192 is a compute-optimized server instance belonging to the c4n family. It features 192 dedicated vCPUs built on the x86_64 architecture and is configured with 384 GB of system memory. This configuration establishes a memory-to-vCPU ratio of 2.0 GB per core, prioritizing raw processing capacity over memory density.

This server type does not include local storage or integrated GPU hardware, meaning all storage requirements must be met via network-attached volumes. Additionally, the instance does not include complimentary public IPv4 addresses. These design choices focus the hardware profile entirely on compute-bound workloads, eliminating the overhead of local storage controllers and accelerator hardware.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the c4n-highcpu-192 offers high compute resource density for parallel processing tasks. The dedicated CPU allocation ensures consistent execution times without resource contention. The server is designed for compute-heavy workloads such as high-performance computing, large-scale build systems, batch processing, and highly parallelized CPU-bound simulations that do not require local SSD storage or GPU acceleration.
